evidence_level: full original numeric MAT member, all 363 robot state members; companion full text checked
findings: 363 robot-state MAT files, 181 under slot 1 and 182 under slot 2. Each contains states.ATIFT_plate, states.ATIFT_wrist, and states.FT in six columns, as well as position and rotation, measured and reference joint position/speed, and measured and external joint-torque fields. All three six-channel fields are finite for all 13,433 rows. Exactly 362 files have 37 rows and one has 39. The 363 MAT payload hashes and datetime suffixes differ.

The source paper reports 180 data entries (three attempts in each of 40 failure conditions plus 60 nominal). The archive contains both slots. Each has 60 nominal captures and three per nonzero offset except x−1 mm with 4 files in slot 1 and 5 in slot 2. Some repeat index numbers have different datetime suffixes; multiplying the paper count by two misses three published captures. No claim is made that these archive captures are statistically independent.

In 7,367 adjacent row pairs states.t repeats (6,066 distinct t values summed within files). For every repeated pair the ATIFT_plate vector and the ATIFT_wrist vector each change, while FT stays exactly unchanged. states.trun strictly increases within all 363 files. Dropping repeated t rows would discard new plate and wrist readings. This outcome does not determine the individual hardware clocks or lags.

At a descriptive plate-force-norm threshold of 5, 223 of 363 files cross it. The threshold is applied in the native reported values and differs from the article’s 10 N z-direction stop. In nominal (zero commanded positional offset) files, 0/60 slot 1 and 47/60 slot 2 cross 5. The slot split makes the threshold unsuitable as a universal failure label.

For each file crossing 5, summarize all rows before the first crossing with plate norm at or below 0.5/1/2. Across those ceilings the eligible files are 195/219/223 and the eligible rows 1,979/4,228/6,753. At ceiling 1 the across-file median of the within-file medians is 0.555011 for plate-force norm, 2.277396 for wrist-force norm, and 0.019142 for wrist-moment norm. These are an operational low-load comparison at the same recorded rows; they are not a calibration offset vector.
limitations: The article identifies the ATI Delta underneath the plate as the primary force sensor in the peg-in-hole task. It names the wrist ATI Nano25 for the separate ring task. A nonconstant field named ATIFT_wrist is present in these peg records, but its identity, coordinate transform, tare procedure, unit convention and latency are not verified from the archive. FT differs from both named ATI fields. Native component norms are reported without rotation or unit conversion.

The release contains no explicitly identified unloaded electronic bias vector, tare timestamp, certified free-contact interval, independent first-touch switch, or independently calibrated contact wrench at the wrist. Low plate-load is a descriptive condition. Values also depend on object weight, mounting, reference frame, insertion conditions and filtering.

The zero folder is zero commanded Cartesian offset, not zero force. A 5-unit norm threshold is distinct from the published stopping criterion of 10 N along z; there is no inference about controller success based on our threshold. Matching auxiliary filenames does not verify marker/image values or alignment.

outputs.pih-trials.csv: Per member SHA-256, capture count, repeated time checks and paired six-axis norm summaries. Row indices are zero-based. Force uses first three components, moment uses last three.
outputs.pih-baseline-sensitivity.csv: At each of three plate-force-norm ceilings, within-file medians for selected rows preceding the first crossing of 5. Empty medians mean ineligible.
outputs.pih-conditions.csv: Trial count, row count and number crossing the audit threshold grouped by slot and commanded position error.
outputs.audit_pih.py: Reproduction requires scipy and numpy and the pinned public ZIP. Standard-library zipfile checks member CRC on decompression; the full archive MD5 is compared to Zenodo.
